w: Nine thousand of Cuenca's ten thousand residents could once fit inside this cathedral, begun in 1885 by friar Juan Bautista Stiehle. Its towers were left truncated after a calculation error showed the planned height would overload the foundations -- but the blue-and-white domes became the city's skyline symbol anyway.
s: A cathedral whose towers were cut short by a math error.
_facts: Designed by Juan Bautista Stiehle, a German-born friar who arrived from Alsace in 1873
Construction ran from 1885 for almost a century
Domes covered in blue-and-white glazed tile from Czechoslovakia
Towers left truncated: full planned height would have overloaded the foundations
Could originally seat 9,000 of Cuenca's then 10,000 residents

w: Also known as the Sagrario Church, this mid-16th-century temple was colonial Cuenca's main place of worship until it grew too small and the congregation moved to the New Cathedral across the square. It now serves as the Museum of Religious Art, and remains the only church in the center with a bellows organ.
s: Cuenca's first cathedral, now a museum of altars.
_facts: Was the main Spanish place of worship during colonial Cuenca
Now functions as the Museum of Religious Art
Only church in the historic center with a bellows organ (no longer in service)
